title: Fluency: one term of a bracket's power

families.prompt: What is the number in front of ${v}^{{{e}}}$ in $({v}{b:+})^{{{n}}}$?

wrong.line: That is only the count of paths. Each path also multiplies {ne} copies of {b}.
You raised {b} to the power {e}. The ${v}^{{{e}}}$ term takes {b} from the other {ne} brackets.

solution: The ${v}^{{{e}}}$ term takes ${v}$ from {e} brackets and {b} from the other {ne}.

families.skill: find a coefficient when the letter has a number in front
families.prompt: What is the number in front of ${v}^{{{e}}}$ in $({a}{v}{b:+})^{{{n}}}$?

wrong.line: You used {a} once. Each of the {e} brackets that gives ${a}{v}$ gives a {a}, so you need ${a}^{{{e}}}$.
You left out the {a} in ${a}{v}$. The power of ${a}{v}$ is ${a}^{{{e}}}{v}^{{{e}}}$.

solution: The ${v}^{{{e}}}$ term takes ${a}{v}$ from {e} brackets and {b} from the other {ne}.

families.skill: find the term with no letter
families.prompt: What is the term with no ${v}$ in $\left({a:c}{v}{s:+c}\dfrac{{{m}}}{{{v}}}\right)^{{{n}}}$?

wrong.line: That is only the count of paths. Each path also multiplies the numbers in the two parts.
You left out the count. $\binom{{{n}}}{{{h}}}$ paths each give this term.

solution: The ${v}$ cancels when ${a:c}{v}$ comes from {h} brackets and $\dfrac{{{b}}}{{{v}}}$ from the other {h}.
